facts.fact: Mark 死后两周，Manhattan Remediation 的传单真的塞进了门缝（与 Star/Annie 所说一致）；若非她们提过，她会随手扔掉。
facts.anchor: It was stuck under my door, just like Star and Annie had said.

facts.fact: 传单症状清单（穿堂风、阴影、冷水、声响）其实适用于任何 downtown 公寓；高明在于暗示闹鬼而不点破——Julie 说得对：把房东失职包装成超自然。
facts.anchor: This list of complaints could obviously describe any apartment downtown.

facts.fact: 新迁入者对街区的恐惧写在肢体上：护住钱包、冲进门反锁；不仅是怕抢劫老鼠，更弥散地怕「看见落魄者威胁到自己走运」。
facts.anchor: as if seeing someone down on their luck was a threat to their own.

facts.fact: 她承认自己反复琢磨：谁能对鬼做什么？不看行不行？——但盲视不是隐喻（François 死前失明的现实教训）。
facts.anchor: But blindness, I had newly learned, wasn’t a metaphor.

facts.fact: 见鬼的机制：鬼真实「在那边」——不是此处的反面、只是「偏一点」；须同时看两个平面，像立体画，只是眼见的把戏是真的。
facts.anchor: You have to be able to see two planes at once.

facts.fact: 楼下 Mrs. Vélez 生前死后都跟她聊同一套故事（护士女儿从不来探望）；她不介意，反正有时间听——Mark 数月后才知道 Vélez 已死。
facts.anchor: She was always telling me about her oldest daughter, the nurse practitioner, who I never saw come to visit, but Mrs. Vélez showed me pictures.

facts.fact: 「我」从不见母亲的鬼：那是一种保护，如同幼时 Ruthie 放她独自乱跑、相信爱足以护她周全。
facts.anchor: I do think that I don’t see my mother because she’s protecting me—but in her own way, the way she did when I was little and she let me run around on my own as if her love were enough to keep me safe.

facts.fact: 母亲在 Frick 的绘画课：竖线、横线、斜切线制造 tension，让画有趣——这套「看」的训练日后成了见鬼的眼睛。
facts.anchor: Then my mother made slashes through the air: her jaw, her hair pulled back, her forearm. This creates tension in the painting, she said, and that makes the picture interesting.

facts.fact: Ruthie 本可能是 downtown 女画家：辍学、生女、毒品三选一都够毁掉她；她会讲画好在哪，却无法为自己画出好画。
facts.anchor: My mother went to Music & Art and probably could have been one of those downtown woman painters if she hadn’t dropped out, or if she hadn’t had me, or if she hadn’t got into junk.

facts.fact: Mark 病中整夜出汗、低声抽气地哭了一个月；他说「给我讲讲那幅画吧」——那一刻她知道有多糟，想起 O'Hara：看你胜过世上所有肖像。
facts.anchor: There was a month where he cried a lot, not dramatically, wailing or moaning, just low little gasps that have stayed with me in my dreams more than Mark himself has. “Will you tell me the painting?”

facts.fact: 母亲教的「注意」全在训练她看见静止目光下显形之物；画得越多，鬼越完整地出现。
facts.anchor: All the noticing my mother taught me—the lines, the tension, the curves—was training me to see what materialized when my eye was very still.

facts.fact: 她试图凭记忆画 Mark「画到他活过来」，却总画错；格纹本像栏杆把他隔远——额头新纹（Bianca 能像掌纹一样读出 broken lines—trouble）更接近他死时的样子。
facts.anchor: I had a gridded notebook that I used for sketches, but the more I tried to draw his face, the more it felt like the grid was keeping him from me, as if his face were withdrawing behind the bars.
